name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Heavy outside spending opposing the Democratic nominee but in a lopsided district
model.rationale: The district's +22 Democratic lean and the fundamentals pointing to a roughly 30-point Democratic edge make this a Safe D race, and Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 96%. Outside spending against Oliver Gilbert is notable but unlikely to overcome the district's partisan makeup.
model.watch: A further surge in outside spending against Gilbert or an unusually strong Republican turnout environment could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves this Miami-area seat open, but the district's strong Democratic lean of +22 points keeps it firmly in the party's column. Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown and enters as the clear favorite, though outside groups have spent heavily opposing him.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat, and no general-election polls contradict that picture. With no expert ratings available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin of around 24 points.
